content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The written test is mandatory, and all applicants may sit it without their eligibility being checked first. Those who qualify go on to the Skill Test. The minimum marks are: Candidates who reach these marks move to the checking of eligibility and documents verification. Candidates found eligible by the Screening Committee and shortlisted by the University are called for documents verification, while those declared ineligible are not informed of their status. The structure and syllabus of the test will be uploaded on the University website in due course. Marks are given individually through the applicant login or by email. Any objections will be invited by displaying the question paper and answer key on the website. Candidates in the blindness, locomotor disability (both arm affected) and cerebral palsy categories can have a scribe or compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour, if they want it. A scribe is provided only if they apply for the facility in the online form. If the online form has no such provision, the applicant must submit the application at least 07 days before the scheduled date of the written test. Other benchmark disability categories need a certificate of physical limitation to write from a Medical Board of the Chief Medical Officer and at least two other members of a Government health care institution. They must apply in the online form and upload the certificate as per Annexure-D. The scribe's qualification should be one step below the minimum qualification prescribed for the post, and the scribe must not be a candidate in the same examination. The scribe must produce a valid ID proof in original at the examination. A photocopy signed by the candidate and the scribe is submitted with the proforma. A candidate using their own scribe gives a letter of undertaking in the format at Annexure-E. No attendant other than the scribe is allowed inside the exam hall.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The posts are to be filled on a regular basis, at Functional Pay Level FPL-6 under the 7th CPC. Any advertised post may be withdrawn at any stage without assigning a reason, and the University may choose not to fill any of the posts. If the recruitment is not completed within six months, the posts will be re-advertised. If an inadvertent mistake in selection is detected at any stage, even after the appointment letter is issued, the University may modify, withdraw or cancel any communication made to the applicant. No TA/DA is paid for attending any written test, skill test, presentation or interview. All disputes are subject to the jurisdiction of Palwal Court only.

If the NOC is delayed, they can apply directly with the experience certificate and submit the NOC at Document Verification.

faq.question: Q1. Which discipline has the most Skill Instructor vacancies?
faq.answer: CSE/IT has the most, with 10 posts under Advt. No. T-42/2026. Agriculture and Medical Lab. Technology follow with 03 each.

faq.question: Q2. Can a diploma holder apply for SVSU Skill Instructor posts?
faq.answer: Yes, in some disciplines. Civil, Electrical, Electronics and Mechanical (RAC), for example, accept a first class three-year Engineering Diploma with six years' experience.

faq.question: Q3. Is a National Trade Certificate accepted?
faq.answer: Yes, for Civil, Electrical, Electronics, Hospitality, Mechanical (RAC) and Printing & Technology. These need eight years' experience, including the training period.

faq.question: Q4. Can candidates from outside Haryana apply?
faq.answer: Yes, but a reserved-category applicant from another state is considered only against General posts and pays Rs. 1000/-.

faq.question: Q5. Can I apply for more than one discipline?
faq.answer: Yes. Each post needs its own application and its own fee.

faq.question: Q6. Is my eligibility checked before the written test?
faq.answer: No. All applicants may appear in the written test, and eligibility is checked only after a candidate qualifies both tests.

faq.question: Q7. What marks must a General candidate score to reach document verification?
faq.answer: A General candidate needs 40% in each test and 50% cumulative marks across the written and skill tests.

faq.question: Q8. I am a government employee and my NOC is delayed. Can I still apply?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply directly with your experience certificate and hand in the NOC from your present employer at Document Verification.

faq.question: Q9. Will test dates be published in newspapers?
faq.answer: No. The dates of any test or interview and the shortlisted lists will be posted on the University website.

faq.question: Q10. Which registration is mandatory for health science posts?
faq.answer: Nursing needs State Nursing Council registration, Pharmacy needs State Pharmacy Council registration, and Physiotherapy needs registration with the State council/NCAHP.
